newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates firm, demand strong.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates firm, demand strong.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates held firm on Wednesday on strong demand despite improved liquidity of the banking sector, dealers said.
They put money market settlements at a high 40.3 million kuna by 0915 GMT, with more term loans than usual.
Call money was granted at a steady 8.0 percent with term rates ranging between 11 percent for 10-day deals to 18 percent on 90-day kuna.
Banks ended Tuesday with 496 million kuna in their accounts and no shortfalls. They had 14.5 million in outstanding Lombard loans from the central bank.
"Cutting reserve requirement really helped but banks are also say their deposit base has increased," said one dealer.
The banking sector today invested 96 million kuna in new central bank paper, used as a voluntary instrument for sterilising money supply.

Liquidity is expected to get another boost before the weekend, when the central bank pays kuna to banks for the hard currency it has purchased at today's auction. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
